analysis: Examined the SSD hybrid checkpoint read path changes (T-041, TB-007, A-001). (1) SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Read.swift lines 128-129 and 203-204: restore accesses are now created with mode .shared, so concurrent same-file reads proceed. Writers and maintenance still need exclusive or try-acquire leases. The Access/coordinator implementation (makeAccess mode, tryUpgrade, downgrade) is not in the supplied evidence, so shared-versus-exclusive semantics are an unverified contract. (2) ReadAttempt.swift lines 96-100: corrupt-file removal now runs only when this reader is the sole holder, via a non-blocking upgrade for the leaf or a free exclusive lease for an ancestor. A corrupt or tampered file can therefore stay indexed while other readers hold it. Reads still fail on AES-GCM/AAD authentication, and the authenticated identity receipt (lines 216, 67) is unchanged, so this is a transient availability or cleanup delay with no confidentiality or integrity regression. Corrupt files still age out under the TTL. (3) persistRecency, lines 132-148: the mtime touch is skipped when the file is fresher than ttl/30 and happens only under sole-holder access. It runs before the second openChain that records identity (line 206-209), so the touch does not invalidate the receipt. The ordering holds. recencyRefreshSeconds is 0 if ttlSeconds < 30, so every hit would try a touch. That is a performance and ctime-churn edge, not a security issue. (4) SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove (lines 75-78, 94-99) and SSDPrefixCache.swift lines 1790-1800: the new optional unusedSince defers TTL deletion when the in-memory index saw a hit more recently, and persists the mtime without moving it backward. This can extend retention only up to the index's own sliding TTL, which matches the existing sliding-TTL semantics. It does not exceed the 30-minute bound unless callers pass a wrong unusedSince. Callers of retireOwnedEntries(unusedSince:) are not in the supplied evidence, so integration should check the TTL sweep passes now - ttl. index.lastAccess is not shown. No new data exposure, key handling, or plaintext paths. HMAC-keyed names, AAD and the KEK chain are untouched.
